text:
maria: Pushed a new docs PR for the troubleshooting guide: trimming strategies, retry/backoff patterns, and a pragmatic model-fallback example. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4190. Hoping for lightweight reviews — want to ship before tomorrow's docs sync.

alex: Skimming now. Quick Q: should the trimming approaches live under the "limits" page or be a short standalone appendix? We get lost when the same advice is duplicated.

maria: Plan is standalone appendix: "Practical fixes for token limits". Keeps core pages canonical and lets us iterate on examples without touching core narratives.

tj: One immediate ask: the JS sample in the draft still shows the old client.stream() helper. We deprecated that in favor of client.responses.stream / responses.create. I can send a tiny patch to switch examples and keep both streaming + non-streaming variants.

alex: Also add a concrete example that reads Retry-After and falls back to exponential backoff when missing. People often assume Retry-After is always present, which causes weird loops.

rachel: CI flagged examples/trim_guide.md for import path issues in the python snippet (using redwood_sdk.client instead of redwood.client).

docs-bot: markdown-link-check failed on examples/appendix.md: https://old-docs.redwood.ai/model-variants -> 404.

maria: Thanks, will update the model-variants slug and fix the python import right now.

maria: Pushed fixes: corrected python import to "from redwood import Client as RedwoodClient", updated model-variants link to /models/variants, and replaced deprecated JS method. Commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/def456

tj: Nice cleanup. I left two tiny comments: 1) In the Python retry snippet you use param "timeout_secs" but our SDK expects "timeout" (seconds). 2) For the fallback-to-cheaper-model example, add a short note about evaluation: cheaper models may change safety/accuracy — encourage running your prompt-suite.

maria: Added a short "tradeoffs" note referencing the evals playbook and changed timeout param to "timeout" in the py snippet. Also added a tiny JS sync example using responses.create for short calls and an async streaming example using responses.stream.

alex: Suggest we show a capped backoff with jitter. Something like:

```py
ra = int(resp.headers.get("Retry-After", "0"))
if ra > 0:
    sleep(ra)
else:
    backoff = min(BASE * (2 ** attempt), MAX_BACKOFF)
    backoff = backoff * random.uniform(0.5, 1.5)  # jitter
    sleep(backoff)
```

alex: That prevents synchronous thundering retries.

rachel: Agreed. I also asked for a short note near the top: "When to prefer graceful degradation vs immediate retry" (i.e., if user-facing latency SLO is tight, prefer graceful degrade to a smaller model or trimmed prompt).

maria: Good point. I added a short decision checklist at the top of the appendix with three cases: retry, trim, fallback.

docs-bot: lint-check passed for examples/trim_guide.md. markdown-link-check still warning on external link to third-party tokenizer tool (we should vendor the snippet or host a sanitized example).

tj: I'll remove the external link and copy a minimal tokenizer example into /examples/code/tokenize_helper.{js,py}.

maria: Thanks — pushed that and updated references. PR updated to https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4190#issuecomment-1

alex: LGTM from me aside from one belated nit about wording in the tradeoffs paragraph. Small grammar fix suggested.

tj: Fixed the param name in Python and approved.

docs-bot: PR #4190 merged by maria at 1765556834.

maria: Awesome work team, thanks! If we want a diagram for the decision checklist I can file a follow-up issue and we can sketch in the next docs pairing session. :sparkles:
